# Consolidation value: current-reserve accounting

**Snapshot headline: 0 additional narratives clear the spec’s 85.018013680 SOL trigger by pooling current reserves.** Reserve-weighted copy-money share c is **6.32% across all SOL text groups**, including singletons, and **10.18% among multi-member copy clusters**. Both figures include completed and uncompleted groups.

This is a conservative snapshot accounting result under fixed cashflows and grouping, not an estimate that lifetime consolidation gain is zero. Current reserves cannot exceed a cluster’s historical aggregate peak. Past higher reserves could add candidates; how many is unmeasured and the historical count may equal the bound. Actual production graduation is also affected by the liveness gate and shared-market behaviour, so this is not an unconditional lower bound on real product outcomes.

The 62 groups with a completed member already produced a fragmented-market completion and contribute **no additional graduation**. The 952 groups with no completed member are the headline population. The former group enters measured c only; no larger-room or incremental-graduation claim is made from its pooled balances.

## Corrections applied

A completed curve’s zero reserve is not a failed launch or lost outcome: completion is the baseline success flag, and verified pool reserve restores its money for c. Waiting pool fees and virtual boost are excluded. Uncompleted does not imply the production liveness gate passes. The full quote mix replaces the earlier subsample approximation; no non-SOL reserve is treated as lamports. The conservative count may equal its historical counterpart; “strictly higher” is not established.

## Cohort and measurements

The original 2956 launches span 1.72 hours. Every curve was read: 2213 SOL quotes retained; 743 other quotes (25.14%) excluded, with no mixed-asset conversion. Exact v1 folded-identity/name equality forms 1014 groups, including 283 multi-member clusters. No URI, social, image, symbol-only, fuzzy or assistant-semantic labels alter grouping.

Initial curve reads: finalized slots 464129076–464129301. Refined balances: slots 464133181–464133472, 2026-11-01T14:55:10.836209+00:00 to 2026-11-01T14:56:11.654471+00:00. All accounts within each group share one RPC context; different groups use sequential snapshots.

All 81 completed SOL members have verified canonical pools. Member reserve means the curve’s real SOL reserve plus migrated real WSOL pool reserve. For pools, real reserve is vault token amount minus waiting protocol/creator fees; virtual boost is excluded. Waiting fees excluded total 0.206504488 SOL. Raw curve, pool and vault bytes, owners, timestamps and slots are cached. See the [official fee/reserve identity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pump-fun/pump-public-docs/639b87fb45c3adeffa6f7c4a1bf0cb85e392bf22/docs/VIRTUAL_QUOTE_RESERVES_FEE_ADJUSTMENT.md).

USD is a fixed normalisation at **$95.045/SOL**, Coinbase observation 2026-11-01T14:40:30.312355+00:00 ([source](https://api.coinbase.com/v2/prices/SOL-USD/spot)). It is not a historical USD valuation or a market-cap threshold. The spec trigger is derived from its curve default plus graduation rent and checked against §2; it remains a Config value copied into each Room, not a new hardcoded program constant.

## Copy-money share c

`c = (sum of member reserves − largest member reserve) / sum of member reserves`. The pooled weighted mean is Σ(nonlargest reserve)/Σ(total reserve), not an average of group percentages. Zero-total groups have undefined c and are excluded from percentiles; their zero weight does not change the weighted mean. This is a current reserve-stock share, including migrated liquidity, not a measured lifetime gross-spending split; buying, selling, fees and liquidity changes can alter it.

The money split is $10,000 of total current cluster reserve, using the same fixed price. It distinguishes funded narratives from dust, and includes both completion classes. Copy-only rows avoid a median dominated by singletons; all-group rows represent the whole observed SOL population.

Concentration matters: 94.07% of off-largest reserve sits in one already-completed text group. Its root mint is `mCvz6xFN5W26ej8uAaUWtZFAtXWss7gJF1hYvJTpump`. This is an observed concentration, not a reason to remove the group or relabel it; it limits extrapolation from this window.

## Tail fit and predicted versus counted multipliers

Fit the **survival exponent** α in P(M≥x) ∝ x^−α, where M is each group’s largest member reserve, so the unit is the same narrative counted in the threshold table. The density exponent is α+1. Continuous Pareto MLE chooses xmin by minimum descriptive KS with a declared minimum tail size. A shifted exponential is fitted to the same selected tail for a conditional AIC comparison.

| population | xmin SOL | xmax SOL | tail n | α | Pareto KS | exponential KS | Pareto AIC | exponential AIC |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All groups, both completion classes | 0.273058 | 6716.19 | 101 | 0.472582 | 0.077815 | 0.817224 | 520.638 | 1300.304 |
| Groups with no completed member | 0.00386087 | 44.9403 | 200 | 0.381100 | 0.082699 | 0.567161 | -385.274 | 338.927 |

**All groups, both completion classes:** A Pareto is a serviceable descriptive fit over the selected observed tail, not a validated population law.

**Groups with no completed member:** A Pareto is a serviceable descriptive fit over the selected observed tail, not a validated population law.

These are in-sample descriptive fits, not calibrated goodness-of-fit tests. Cutoff and α are chosen on the same observations; no simulated/bootstrap p-value is claimed. The cutoff is selected for the Pareto, so the conditional AIC comparison is not an independent family-selection test. The no-completion cohort is selected against high historical reserves and is truncated by completion/migration, making unbounded extrapolation particularly weak. Cutoff-sensitivity fits and sample ranges are in the JSON report.

The fitted survival exponents at or below one (All groups, both completion classes, Groups with no completed member) imply no finite mean for the ideal unbounded Pareto. Actual capital is finite. Together with observed concentration, this is another reason not to extrapolate the finite-window weighted c as a universal input.

The formula (1−c)^−α gives 1.031359× using the whole-population c and tail, but that population includes already completed narratives. For the eligible no-completion cohort, its own c and tail give 1.008353×. Only the latter is a like-population comparison for the headline. Neither is evidence of larger post-graduation rooms. A constant c, an untruncated power-law tail, and stable group composition are assumptions of that formula; the observed c varies by group.

| diagnostic threshold USD | SOL | largest above | sum above | new candidates | counted multiplier | same-cohort formula | inside selected observed tail? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| $10.00 | 0.105213 | 65 | 66 | 1 | 1.015385× | 1.008353× | True |
| $100.00 | 1.052133 | 23 | 23 | 0 | 1.000000× | 1.008353× | True |
| $1,000.00 | 10.521332 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 1.000000× | 1.008353× | True |

The required graduation/high-dollar cuts have no eligible largest-member or pooled exceedances, so their counted multiplier is undefined, not one. Lower diagnostic cuts are shown to expose the counting comparison; they do not stand for a narrative that caught on. Where a scalar formula differs from the finite counts, the counts win. Variable c, cohort selection, a selected/censored tail and discrete small counts explain why the formula need not reproduce them. This does not validate a universal multiplier.

## Limits

- **Gate coverage:** 1085 of 1199 conditional text-copy joins are within the configured grace; 114 need missing historical reserve, idle, volume or pool-checkpoint state. Current account reads cannot substitute for launch-time histories. Uncompleted is not the same as gate-live. Main groups use exact v1 text equality with an explicit all-live accounting assumption; the grace-prefix column uses only the in-window root’s protected prefix. No production-gated point estimate is claimed.
- **Pre-window roots:** the true truncated-root count is unknown. Every observed root lies in this sample by construction; that is not evidence that no earlier matching room existed. Grace diagnostics condition on an empty in-window replay boundary.
- **Age:** member reserves were read at 21.754–23.462 hours after launch (median 22.602). No invented fixed-age or linear age correction is applied. Older launches had more time to both attract buying and experience selling; the raw snapshot is not a launch-age-controlled comparison.
- **Window:** one short contiguous, Halloween-season sample cannot establish long-run fragmentation, rare narratives or lifetime economic value. No semantic labels are invented: these are operational text groups, not independently adjudicated narratives.
- **Counterfactual:** the accounting assumes the same buyers spend the same amounts, with member cashflows/withdrawals and grouping held fixed. A shared curve changes slippage, selling, routing, fees and incentives, which this measurement cannot capture.
- **Reaching versus holding:** the earlier simulation in `DESIGN.md` found shared curves could drain faster when holders take profit together. It is not new measurement here. This study counts current accounting threshold opportunities, not how long a shared room would hold them or how large an already graduated room would become.

## Reproduce

```bash
python3 scripts/narrative/collect_consolidation_outcomes.py --collect
python3 scripts/narrative/collect_consolidation_balances.py --collect
python3 scripts/narrative/measure_consolidation_value.py
```

Collectors resume their cached run without replacing completed observations. The measurement command is offline and uses only the standard library. Source hashes, complete per-group/member data and fit details are in `outputs/narrative/consolidation_value.json`; the CSV lists every group’s maximum, sum, completion class and c.
